title: Evidence streamlining playbook for SOC2/ISO and identity hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: deliver a repeatable milestone tracker + lightweight automation that reduces manual evidence collection for SOC2 and ISO certification cycles and simultaneously hardens identity (SSO/SAML) auditability. Scope includes: mapping evidence types to telemetry sources (console actions, API keys, dedicated cluster events, user provisioning), implementing an evidence ingestion pipeline (producer -> durable event store -> transformer -> evidence bundles), establishing retention/archival policies for audit logs, and producing a testable SSO/SAML verification matrix for auditors. Deliverables: 1) Evidence mapping spec (CSV + Confluence) for top 25 controls; 2) Event tagging schema and producer libs for console/SDK; 3) Proof-of-concept evidence pipeline that emits signed evidence bundles to secure object store; 4) Audit log retention and replay guide; 5) SSO/SAML hardening checklist and verification tests for auditors; 6) Milestone tracker with owners, gating criteria, and roll-forward plan. Success metrics: reduce manual evidence hours by 70% for a compliance cycle, 100% deterministic traceability for SSO events in the evidence bundle, automated generation of at least 60% of required SOC2 artifacts. Out of scope: full certification run, third-party auditor liaison, and long-term archival (beyond 7 years). Stakeholders: Security (Marta Ruiz), Platform (Ravi Singh), Console PM (Liam Chen), Runtime Eng lead (Sofia Ortega), Legal (Nina Park).

acceptance_criteria: Top-25 control evidence mapping document exists and is owner-assigned
Producer libraries for Console and SDK produce schema v0.1 events with example payloads
Evidence pipeline assembles signed bundles and writes to configured regional object stores
Audit log retention policy implemented as configurable lifecycle (min 2 years, configurable to 7 years)
SSO/SAML verification matrix with pass/fail tests mapped to auditor expectations
Milestone tracker updated weekly with owners, status, and blockers and a runbook for auditor handoff
risks_and_blockers: KMS key provisioning for signing needs alignment with infra schedule (risk: delays could block proof-of-evidence signing)
Event volume and cost: high-cardinality telemetry could blow up storage costs if not deduped early
Cross-region residency requirements for EU customers complicate a single global sink
Dependence on Identity team's SAML assertion logs formatting (need contract/format agreement)
Auditor expectations may require additional data retention and chain-of-custody guarantees beyond PoC
